messages.author: 559201f5f605d5a7
messages.subject: Semi-landmark placement issue (buildtemplate & digitsurface)
parts:
Hi All,

I am a novice R user and new to the geomorph package, and I'm having some issues with semi-landmark placement through the buildtemplate and digitsurface functions. I'm trying to place semi-landmarks on PLY meshes of Acheulean Handaxes (stone tools), although the digitsurface function doesn't seem to distribute semi-landmarks on mesh surfaces well. In fact, when I use this function, semi-landmark tend to either clump in areas, or scatter across space (i.e. not making contact with mesh surfaces).

One issue I suspect is causing problems is that there are no real homologous points in which to plot true landmarks aside from the tip and base of these meshes. There's much debate about the use of landmarks on stone tools as they vary in size and shape, which makes consistency in landmark placement through the buildtemplate function an issue.

So far, I've tried placing 10 landmarks in buildtemplate long the edge of a scan, evenly spaced from the point to the base. Although when I try to plot landmarks in digitsurface, the semi-landmarks scatter through space. Again, I'm very new to R and geomorph, so any help or advice would be greatly appreciated!!

Cheers!

messages.author: 4c2b8549469e242c
messages.subject: Re: Semi-landmark placement issue (buildtemplate & digitsurface)
parts:
Hi Matt, 

I could be completely wrong, but I've had a similar issue with digitsurface and it seemed to have something to do with the mesh itself and how I decimated it. I had a look at my mesh in Meshlab and looked at where the triangle vertices were, and it turned out I had lumps of triangle summits in the same areas where digitsurface lumped semi-landmarks together. If I remember correctly, using a non-decimated mesh with regularly spaced vertices to build the template helped correct this issue.

I hope this helps,
Best, 

Lou

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Semi-landmark placement issue (buildtemplate & digitsurface)
parts:
Dear Matt and Lou,

You are correct - it is about the mesh vertices and how they are distributed. The algorithm beneath the semilandmarks template function is using the vertices of the meshes themselves to find equally spaced semilandmarks (via kmeans). Therefore, if the mesh is not homogenous in terms of the vertices, you will get an odd looking result.

Meshlab can remesh your files easily.

Em
